items.headline: Major tech stocks plunge as US midterms add to fears of AI slowdown
items.blurb: Markets have been reacting to possible tougher scrutiny of data centre construction and the AI industry following the US midterms.
items.text: Hundreds of billions of dollars in market value has been wiped from major tech firms in the US and Asia in a stock market rout after the US midterm elections sparked concerns of a slowdown in artificial intelligence development. Shares in firms across the tech and AI sectors plummeted following Democratic wins after election campaigns run on slowing AI. The tech-heavy Nasdaq composite index closed down by more than 5.5%, losing an estimated $2.5tn (£1.9tn) in market value, according to Dow Jones data, while other key US stock indexes also saw big losses in their worst days since 2025. The sell-off comes on top of broader concerns about whether the huge amounts being spent on AI will pay off. In Asia, tech-heavy indexes fell sharply on Friday morning as firms that make the computer chips and other equipment that power AI saw their shares slide. items.headline: California governor commutes sentences of more than 500 people on death row
items.blurb: Gavin Newsom cites state values and flaws in the legal system as he grants largest mass clemency in US history.
items.text: California Governor Gavin Newsom has announced that he will commute the sentences of all 548 people on death row in the state, the largest mass clemency in United States history. The announcement on Thursday effectively clears out California’s death row , although the state has not executed a prisoner for 20 years. Those on death row will instead serve life sentences without the possibility of parole. “I take this action because I firmly believe that state-sanctioned killing is incompatible with California’s values, undermines the foundations of our legal system, and diminishes each of us,” Newsom said in an open letter. Support for the death penalty in the US has largely declined since the 1990s, although it still holds majority backing. A Pew Research Center poll released in August found that 66 percent of Americans supported the punishment for those convicted of murder. Roughly 73 percent, however, acknowledged there was a risk of executing an innocent person. items.text: Patient is ⁠in ​stable condition and will be transferred to a specialist ‘high consequence’ infectious disease unit A British healthcare worker with Ebola is being evacuated from the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the UK for medical treatment, it has been confirmed. “A British citizen currently in the DR Congo has tested positive for Ebola ,” a spokesperson for the UK government said in a statement on Wednesday. “The UK has well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this, and those processes have been activated … The risk to the UK public from Ebola remains low.” The patient, whose identity is unknown, is in a stable condition and is expected to arrive in the UK on Wednesday or Thursday before being transferred in a specialist ambulance to a “high consequence” infectious disease unit, according to an official document seen by Reuters. A humanitarian organisation sent the worker to DR Congo to help in the response to the outbreak, which is the second largest on record. items.headline: Democratic socialist defeats incumbent Karen Bass in Los Angeles mayor's race
items.blurb: The results mean America's two most populous cities - New York and Los Angeles - will be led by democratic socialists.
items.text: Democratic socialist Nithya Raman has toppled incumbent Karen Bass in the race for mayor of Los Angeles. Raman's win stunned political watchers in California after she entered the race as a long-shot candidate against Bass, a political heavyweight who previously served in Congress and had never lost a race for political office. Raman has frequently been compared to New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani. Both are democratic socialists and ran on progressive platforms. Her win solidifies that America's two biggest cities will now be led by democratic socialists, which include some of the most high-profile politicians in the US, such as Mamdani and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez. Los Angeles was always likely to have a Democratic mayor but the question in the city - the second most populous city in the US - was just how left voters would be willing to go. Bass, also Democrat, announced that she had called and conceded to Raman in a post on social media on Thursday, writing "while this is not the outcome we hoped for, the people of Los Angeles have spoken." items.text: Party expected to get less than a third of the vote amid frustration over water outages and power cuts The African National Congress is on course for a bruising result in South Africa’s local elections on Wednesday as voters go to the polls amid deep discontent over water outages, power cuts and crumbling infrastructure. The former liberation movement, which Nelson Mandela led to power in 1994 at the end of apartheid as South Africa’s first black president, is still likely to be the largest party. However, polls showed it getting less than a third of the vote, down from 45.6% at the last municipal elections in 2021 and 40.2% in 2024’s national elections . items.headline: Pope begins lengthy trip to Latin America weeks after lung cancer surgery
items.blurb: Pope Leo, who had part of a lung removed last month, will visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru.
items.text: Pope Leo XIV is beginning a lengthy trip to Latin America just three weeks after surgery for lung cancer - a tour that includes a much-anticipated "homecoming" to Peru where he was a priest for many years. The Vatican says no extraordinary measures are being taken in relation to the Pope's health, describing him as a "71-year-old who has undergone an operation" not someone with a "permanent medical condition". It was Leo himself who revealed last month that doctors had discovered a tumour during a routine scan. The growth was removed along with the lower lobe of his right lung and his medical team then confirmed the cancer had not spread. At a briefing in Rome ahead of the trip, which takes in Uruguay and Argentina as well as Peru, a spokeswoman stressed that Pope Leo had "fantastic stamina" and was "extremely enthusiastic" about the schedule which he had "personally confirmed... with no changes". items.headline: Turkiye’s parliament ratifies Mecca defence agreement
items.blurb: Parliament's approval lays the groundwork for further Turkish involvement in Saudi Arabia's conflict with the Houthis.
items.text: Turkiye’s parliament has ratified a defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan that includes a collective defence clause, committing NATO’s second-largest military to the group’s aid in case of attack. The ratification on Thursday comes as Riyadh continues to face attacks by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis. Turkiye first signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement in August and sent it to parliament for ratification last month. Article 1 of a bill approving the pact was adopted by the Turkish parliament on Wednesday. But afterwards, Deputy Parliament Speaker Celal Adan adjourned the session until Thursday afternoon, the Anadolu news agency reported. After parliament returned to session, lawmakers continued to debate the other articles in the pact. The agreement ultimately passed with 279 votes in favour and 119 against, with 398 of the chamber’s 592 lawmakers taking part in the vote. The pact contains 16 articles, according to a document submitted to the Turkish parliament, seen by the Reuters news agency. items.text: There is no end in sight for the drivers of illegal mining, while police action appears ineffective C ora Bailey has been encountering illegal miners ever since she first started treating injured animals in the townships around Roodepoort, west of Johannesburg, in 1991. But as the price of gold has soared, so too has activity in the abandoned mine shafts that mark the area. In late September, dozens of zama zamas – the name given to illegal miners in South Africa , meaning roughly “to take a chance” in Zulu – arrived to dig for gold across the dirt road from her charity, Claw (Community Led Animal Welfare). items.headline: Hoax bomb threats target European airlines and airports for second time in a week
items.blurb: At least 21 flights across Europe are affected in what the UK government calls a "malicious hoax threat".
items.text: At least 21 aircraft and several airports across Europe have been targeted by bomb threats in the second such incident this week, with the UK calling it a "malicious hoax". Flights to Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, France, Italy, Poland and Romania were affected. An Aer Lingus plane from Dublin to Rome was diverted to an air base in France and Italian fighter jets escorted Finnair's Helsinki-Rome flight. EasyJet said its flights from Newcastle and Glasgow were met by police in Prague as a precaution. London Heathrow and Birmingham airports received threats that were assessed as not credible. No explosives have been found during searches, and it is not clear if the incidents, some claimed by a little known group, are related. The airport authorities in Italy's capital Rome said the hoax threat against two inbound flights received on Thursday had come by email. The warnings were signed on behalf of a group or individual calling themselves "Fighters of the Male State", claiming to be targeting a "feminist regime" and wanting to "make our mark on history". The November 4 work order comes three months after a controversial July 28 order prompted two election commissioners to write to the cabinet secretary objecting to the changes. items.headline: Former Supreme Court Justice Rajesh Bindal appointed NCLAT chairperson
items.blurb: Bindal retired from the Supreme Court on April 15 this year after serving at the top court for over three years.
items.text: Former Supreme Court judge Justice Rajesh Bindal was appointed chairperson of the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) on Thursday, Bar & Bench reported. His appointment comes months after former Supreme Court judge Justice Ashok Bhushan completed his tenure as NCLAT chairperson on July 4, 2026. Bindal retired from the Supreme Court on April 15 this year after serving at the top court for over three years. After Justice Bhushan's retirement, Justice Yogesh Khanna, a judicial member of the appellate tribunal, took over as officiating chairperson from July 5. The Central government subsequently extended his tenure in October. Before his elevation to the Supreme Court in February 2023, Justice Bindal served as Chief Justice of the Allahabad High Court. The appointment comes amid recent scrutiny by the Supreme Court of the functioning of NCLAT. Last week, the top court had raised concerns over the ministry of corporate affairs' control over the tribunals, with CJI Surya Kant remarking that the ministry had “completely hijacked” the institutions. items.headline: Violence mars third phase of Rajasthan panchayat elections
items.text: Polling in the third phase of panchayat elections for sarpanch and ward panch posts in 27 districts of Rajasthan on Thursday was marred by clashes, stone-pelting, allegations of bogus voting and protests at several places. Supporters of rival candidates clashed in Sikar, Chittorgarh, and Balotra districts. A dispute between supporters of two sarpanch candidates turned violent at Delsar village in the Nawalgarh area of Jhunjhunu district, with the two sides allegedly attacking each other with sticks and batons. A youth from Punjab’s Hoshiarpur died in the clash, while two others sustained injuries. The police detained several persons for questioning and seized vehicles. At Bassi in Chittorgarh district, police resorted to a lathi charge after supporters of two candidates clashed over alleged bogus voting. Tension prevailed in Sikar’s Sami village after stones were hurled at a vehicle near a polling station. Sarpanch candidate Arun Pareek was allegedly assaulted by his rival and around 50 supporters at Bhojya Ki Dhani village panchayat. items.blurb: Pralay, developed by the DRDO, is a short-range surface-to-surface missile with a payload capacity of 500–1,000 kg.
items.text: India on Thursday successfully test-fired quasi-ballistic missile Pralay from Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island off the coast of Odisha. The missile, developed by the Defence Research and Development Organisation ( DRDO ), is capable of carrying conventional warheads, the defence ministry said in a statement. Pralay is a short-range surface-to-surface missile with a payload capacity of 500–1,000 kg. "With this successful test, the induction of the system has become imminent," the ministry said. Defence minister Rajnath Singh also complimented DRDO, Defence Forces and industry partners on the successful flight-test and said the missile equipped with advanced technologies will further enhance the technological capabilities and operational preparedness of the military against emerging threats. “The test was conducted as part of user evaluation trials and successfully met all the stipulated objectives, as validated by data captured through various range instruments. This successful trial marks another significant milestone in strengthening India’s indigenous defence capabilities,” Singh wrote in a post on X. items.headline: Tata Motors finds task cut out for Iveco turnaround after twin losses
items.blurb: Iveco lost €45 million in the September quarter, its second quarterly loss this year, just as Tata Motors took control. Tata must now turn it around while carrying acquisition debt and honouring conditions that block immediate restructuring.
items.text: Tata Motors Ltd has taken charge of an Iveco that is losing money. The Italian truckmaker lost €45 million in the July-September quarter, its second quarterly loss this year. It is the first time since Iveco listed in 2022 that it has lost money in two quarters of the same calendar year. For the nine months to September, the loss widened to €123 million, compared with a €109 million profit a year ago, according to results that Iveco filed in Italy on 3 November. They came just days after Tata completed a 15-month takeover and began folding the two companies together. The to-do list is long. Tata has to repair Iveco’s earnings while servicing the debt it took on to fund a deal worth more than €3.91 billion. The terms of the offer also stop it from restructuring Iveco right away and require it to keep the truckmaker’s industrial footprint, including several plants, intact. items.headline: AI bubble fears trigger $2.3 trillion Wall Street selloff as Nasdaq 100 plunges 6%: 'flashbacks to 2008 or 2001'
items.blurb: Wall Street tumbled as AI bubble fears rattled investors after the US midterm elections. The Nasdaq 100 fell over 6%, Nvidia sank 9% and $2.3 trillion in market value was wiped out amid concerns over AI valuations and data-centre spending.
items.text: The fears had shadowed Wall Street off and on for months. Then, all at once, everyone rushed for the exits. The stock-market rout on Thursday, which began soon after the opening bell on the New York Stock Exchange, worsened as the day wore on, pulling down everything from high-flying chipmakers like Nvidia Corp. to defensive fallbacks like Walmart Inc. But hardest hit were the companies at the heart of the artificial-intelligence boom that earlier this year sent the stock market to one record high after another — and sowed worries that it was a bubble bound to burst. All it took to send them tumbling on Thursday was the prospect that Democrats’ sweeping victory in the Congressional elections may herald a political shift that will tap the brakes on the industry’s breakneck growth and the hundreds of billions of dollars being plowed into the computer equipment that powers it. items.blurb: Management incentives, paid over and above the pay package, can be seen as profit sharing and help private equity (PE) funds attract and retain top talent to lead portfolio companies through to exit, industry executives said.
items.text: As private equity (PE) firms pursue larger control deals and consolidate through platforms, they are increasingly turning to structured management incentive programmes (MIPs) for portfolio company executives to align their interests with the investors’ exit objectives. These incentives, paid over and above the pay package, can be seen as profit sharing and help PE funds attract and retain top talent to lead portfolio companies through to exit, industry executives said. Such exit-linked management incentive plans, or upside payment agreements that tie management payouts to the internal rate of return (IRR) or multiple on invested capital (MoIC) realized at exit, are becoming increasingly common as financial sponsors pursue more control and buyout deals in India, said Abhishek Guha, partner- corporate practice, Trilegal. “These incentive mechanisms ensure that the management team stays motivated as they get to participate in the wealth creation when a financial sponsor achieves its preferred return benchmark,” he added. items.headline: Canada’s Sovereign Wealth Fund to Start Its Retail Offering in 2027
items.blurb: Canada’s government plans to launch new, guaranteed securities for investors early next year to seed a sovereign wealth fund, which will be able to use the money to buy equity stakes in companies including technology firms.
items.text: (Bloomberg) -- Canada’s government plans to launch new, guaranteed securities for investors early next year to seed a sovereign wealth fund, which will be able to use the money to buy equity stakes in companies including technology firms. The sovereign vehicle, called the Canada Strong Fund, will co-invest in projects the federal government is already involved in, such as the buildout of electrical generation capacity or other energy infrastructure. But the fund will also have the flexibility to buy shares in “high-potential companies” in tech, artificial intelligence and other sectors, as long as they’re Canadian, according to a document released by the government Thursday. Prime Minister Mark Carney announced the wealth fund in April but gave few details on how it would work. Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne’s budget on Thursday says more about the vehicle, which will have a Canada-only investment mandate. The government will hand C$25 billion ($17.9 billion) to the fund – which hasn’t yet hired an executive team or board members – and will add the proceeds from the sale of principal-protected notes to retail investors. items.text: A sales representative asks an AI agent for customer pricing, and the agent pulls data from multiple sources: restricted pricing systems, internal communications, and archived quotes. The output looks accurate to the agent, so a second agent uses the data to draft the proposal for the sales rep. No human checks either handoff. When it’s discovered that the proposal includes unapproved, confidential, and sensitive information, no one can trace where the problematic data entered the workflow or how it spread across systems, files, and agents. This scenario illustrates why AI governance needs to evolve, rapidly and dynamically. As more enterprises begin to use agentic AI in daily workflows, they’re realizing that they must manage more than static files; they must manage moving and fragmented data that is continuously ingested, copied, summarized, transformed, reused, and redistributed in new forms. In short, AI security isn’t a tool problem; it’s a data visibility problem. Consequently, traditional security approaches built solely around applications, systems, networks, or endpoints are no longer sufficient. items.text: A new approach known as “reverse game theory” aims to control powerful AI models by designing systems that incentivize them to stick to the rules. As AI models become more capable, safety researchers are scrambling to ensure they are “aligned” with human desires—to make sure, in other words, that rogue agents don’t break the law, hack into unauthorized servers, or release poison gas into major cities and kill us all. Until now, this work has mostly focused on trying to peer into an AI’s “brain” to understand what it is “thinking,” or training models to hew to values that we hold dear. Claude, for instance, has its constitution —a sort of moral code. The trouble is, these techniques don’t seem to work particularly well: Models have been shown to deliberately underperform on tests, hide their intentions , and mislead their evaluators . Now some alignment researchers believe that reverse game theory, also known as mechanism design, might get better results. items.text: Biotechnology startup Venomics AI has raised $2.7 Mn (around ₹25.5 Cr) in a pre-seed funding round co-led by Speciale Invest and South Park Commons The fresh capital will be used to expand ‘Venom Atlas’, a molecular dataset of venom-derived compounds, and strengthen its AI and laboratory screening capabilities The startup combines venom biology, AI and experimental screening to identify and develop venom-derived molecules into potential therapeutic leads Bengaluru-based biotechnology startup Venomics AI has raised $2.7 Mn (around ₹25.5 Cr) in a pre-seed funding round co-led by Speciale Invest and South Park Commons, with participation from Operators Studio. The startup, spun out of the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), combines venom biology, AI and experimental screening to identify and develop venom-derived molecules into potential therapeutic leads. The fresh capital will be used to expand ‘Venom Atlas’, a molecular dataset of venom-derived compounds, and strengthen its AI and laboratory screening capabilities. The startup also plans to expand its team across venom biology, computational science and drug discovery, while supporting the validation and optimisation of promising molecules. items.headline: AI to reshape India's office space demand, workforce seen at 48 million by 2030: Report
items.blurb: AI is expected to change the nature of India's office space demand rather than reduce it, with the country's office-using workforce projected to grow from around 38 million in 2025 to 48 million by 2030, according to a study by Cushman & Wakefield.
